worker_package.objective: Implement and prove the complete Phase 3 Slice 2 minimum branches-and-claims path. Add strict branch creation and immutable branch-head reads; authenticated CLI-agent document or exact-branch claim acquire, renew, release, and claimed authoring; authenticated human branch creation, authoring, and claim revocation; client-retained high-entropy claim secrets with verifier-only SQLite storage; common idempotent control events; document-global revision allocation with branch-head compare-and-swap; and a minimal editor branch/revoke surface using the same versioned client as the CLI. Preserve exact compiler-backed native CSS preview, stable canonical IDs, deterministic exports/receipts, reduced-motion inspection, and the existing locked sole writer. Do not add claim listing, merge/review, annotations, broad collaboration, per-control crash matrices, SSE replay, dirty-draft reconciliation, MCP, Lineage integration, publication, or Phase 4+.

stop_if: Implementation requires any file outside allowed_files, a new npm dependency, package-lock change, or a SQLite import outside packages/local-service/src/sqlite-project-store.ts.
Migration v1 would need to be edited or re-checksummed instead of adding a transactional, backed-up v2 migration that preserves the merged main head and canonical/export digests.
A branch write cannot allocate exactly documents.last_revision+1 while comparing the addressed branch head and preserving pure canonical reduction.
Authentication would rely on actor fields inside the command envelope, URL/query credentials, persisted browser storage, plaintext database secrets, or a generic account/session system.
Acquisition retry cannot be bound privately to the same authenticated context and claim proof while keeping the public operation digest, response, receipt, event, and logs secret-free.

A stale revision, stale lease version, overlap, wrong token/scope, revocation, retry conflict, or injected control fault can consume an operation ID or change any event, branch, claim, lease, document revision, or notification.

The work requires claim listing, merge/review, annotations, broad collaboration, full per-control process-kill coverage, SSE replay, dirty-draft reconciliation, MCP, Lineage integration, publication, or Phase 4+.
The editor or CLI would open SQLite, persist canonical documents or secrets, use a separate reducer/interpolator, address by CSS selector, or bypass the shared protocol client.
Existing deterministic, compiler-native, reduced-motion, browser, privacy, or private-ignore proof must be weakened, skipped, or replaced.
A focused verification command fails twice for the same unresolved product cause.
